title: Underwater Hockey Atlas & Wiki: Rules, Refereeing, Equipment and Safety Library
scope: Curated foundational international and national resources, with medical/safety context and version control. Not an exhaustive global catalogue.
methodology: Primary federation and committee sources were preferred. PDF title pages were checked where retrievable. Records distinguish content inspection, authoritative listings, search-index verification, login restrictions and failed retrieval. A public listing does not establish document currency or permission to reproduce it.
editorial_rules: Keep international CMAS rules, domestic amendments, event-specific bulletins, training aids, research and commercial commentary visibly distinct.
Use current-listed only for a document actually linked by an active authority on the verification date. Do not infer an internal PDF revision from webpage last-updated metadata.
Show date/version, jurisdiction, verification status, checked date, language, access and licence on each resource card.
Link to canonical authority records and offer an identified federation mirror when available. Never silently substitute an older translation.
Use expired/archival labels for old courses, past events and old rule editions. Keep dated referee opportunities separate from evergreen learning resources.
Public accessibility is not an open licence. Link or embed only when permitted; do not mass-copy or rehost rulebooks, lesson slides, illustrations or videos.
Medical resources support education, not individual clearance or treatment. Event protocols, qualified clinicians and trained supervision govern return-to-play and emergency actions.
Do not publish solo underwater breath-hold workouts, hyperventilation routines, maximum-hold challenges or claims of a universally safe submersion duration.

wiki_sections.title: Which rules apply?
wiki_sections.intro: Start with the event's governing authority and published rule edition. The CMAS index currently lists February 2025 rules, and the public v 13.0 PDF combines playing-area and play rules. Domestic rulebooks and event bulletins can add different requirements. Keep the edition and jurisdiction beside every explanation.
wiki_sections.caveat: Never let an old translated PDF appear to supersede the current applicable official text.

wiki_sections.title: Become and develop as a referee
wiki_sections.intro: Refereeing combines rule knowledge, positioning, communication, practical experience and assessment. Begin with the national pathway, then use the CMAS standards to understand international expectations. Video lessons and quick references are study aids; they do not award a qualification.
subtopics: CMAS levels and maintaining active status
Water, chief, timekeeping and scoring roles

wiki_sections.title: Fouls, signals and game management
wiki_sections.intro: Learn signals together with the actual decisions they communicate. Use current rules for sanctions and restarts, and identify the rule edition attached to every clip or diagram. Older lessons remain useful for observation practice but need an instructor's review before being used as current exam material.
wiki_sections.caveat: Books explaining fouls are commentary; they do not override official determinations.

wiki_sections.title: Equipment and playing-area standards
wiki_sections.intro: Separate personal fit and comfort from legal equipment compliance. Inspect the current rulebook and equipment guide before competitions, and check whether local or event requirements differ. Pool geometry, barriers, goals, pucks, protective equipment and team identification each deserve their own checklist.
wiki_sections.caveat: Do not copy quick-start dimensions from federation marketing pages when the rulebook differs.

wiki_sections.title: Safe practice and emergency readiness
wiki_sections.intro: Train and play under competent supervision with a session-specific emergency plan. Never practise underwater breath holding alone or hyperventilate before an underwater effort. Breath-hold contests and ignoring the urge to breathe create avoidable danger. Safety education and hands-on rescue training belong beside skill development.
wiki_sections.caveat: Adjacent freediving material needs hockey context; do not import deep-dive procedures as hockey rules.

wiki_sections.title: Concussion and return to play
wiki_sections.intro: Suspected concussion during an underwater sport warrants prompt removal from play and medical assessment. In-water injury also creates a drowning hazard, so clubs need trained responders and a rehearsed emergency plan. Use the current federation/event protocol and clinician-led return decisions rather than a generic countdown.
wiki_sections.caveat: Some linked national documents are older; version and jurisdiction must be displayed. CMAS policy body could not be retrieved in this pass.

wiki_sections.title: Fitness, injury prevention and reading research
wiki_sections.intro: Conditioning should support movement quality, repeat-effort capacity and recovery without making maximum breath holds the goal. The evidence library separates research findings from tested training programmes. An injury survey can identify priorities, while an observed average submersion time does not establish an individual safe limit.
wiki_sections.caveat: No validated comprehensive UWH-specific conditioning or injury-prevention programme was established in this pass.

wiki_sections.title: Safeguarding, integrity and clean sport
wiki_sections.intro: A complete club resource library includes the responsibilities around play: safeguarding, conduct, risk assessment, anti-doping education and medication checks. These obligations are jurisdiction- and competition-specific. Link current official documents and identify their effective dates instead of rewriting sensitive eligibility rules from memory.

quality_findings.issue: CMAS quick-summary pool dimensions conflict with rulebook
quality_findings.evidence: CMAS landing page says width 15–18m; v 13.0 rule 1.1.2 specifies 12–15m. Cite the rulebook for specifications.
